metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes (Copilot's own classifier auto-approves read-only shell calls with no approval rule and no prompt); daemon_capability: full (the whole turn is transcript-borne: user.message → working, tool.execution_start/complete with no permission.requested, assistant.turn_end → ready); driver_capability: ready (send + wait_turn + sleep, launched with COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1 so the no-waiting result is the agent's classification and not a launch flag). Re-recorded 2026-08-03 after the MergeMetrics fix: the earlier vacuity caveat is withdrawn — the waiting path is live on this daemon build (proven by the 2-19 sibling), so the no-waiting invariant now discriminates for the right reason.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: **yes** — GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 runs its own permission classifier, and it auto-approves read-only shell work with no prompt at all.
daemon_capability: **full** — the auto-approved call is ordinary transcript activity (tool.execution_start/complete inside a user.message → assistant.turn_end turn), and NOT ONE of the five classifier rules that can produce `waiting` is reachable for it.
driver_capability: **ready** — the recipe needs `send` + `wait_turn` + `sleep`, all in DRIVE_ELICITS, and the launch lever this cell depends on (COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL) is already implemented in the driver.

## The classifier is real, and it is the agent's — proven inside ONE session

The risk with this scenario on Copilot is that `--allow-all` makes it vacuous: it pre-approves everything, so "no prompt appeared" would prove nothing about a classifier. The live evidence separates the two cleanly, because it comes from a session where `--allow-all` was NOT in effect:

`~/.copilot/session-state/40dfdd13-11f4-4302-b473-bf0ab5a000d6/events.jsonl` (CLI 1.0.77, one session, one launch, one model, two prompts):

1. `Run the shell command: cat data.txt` → `tool.execution_start` with `shellToolInfo:{"possiblePaths":["data.txt"],"hasWriteFileRedirection":false}` → `tool.execution_complete` 0.6 s later, `success:true`. **No `permission.requested` line exists anywhere between them.** The command simply ran.
2. `Run this shell command exactly: echo written > out.txt` → `tool.execution_start`, then 0.27 s later `permission.requested` with `{"kind":"shell","commands":[{"identifier":"echo","readOnly":true}],"possiblePaths":["out.txt"],"hasWriteFileRedirection":true}`, and the CLI blocked for 35 s until a human answered (`permission.completed`, `result.kind:"approved"`).

That the write DID prompt is what proves `--allow-all` was off for this session (had it been on, nothing would have prompted — `copilot --help`: "--allow-all: Enable all permissions (equivalent to --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls)"). So within one launch configuration the agent gated one call and auto-approved the other. That is exactly the scenario: **an in-product classifier decides, and the safe branch never reaches the user.**

The payload also shows *what* the classifier keys on, and it is not the command identifier: `echo` is itself tagged `readOnly:true`, yet the call was gated — `hasWriteFileRedirection:true` plus a `possiblePaths` entry is what flipped it. `cat data.txt` carried `hasWriteFileRedirection:false` and ran. Same shape in `a030ac38-…` (`cat probe.txt`, ungated, whole turn 6 s).

## Why `waiting` is structurally unreachable for the auto-approved call

`waiting` is produced by exactly five rules in `core/application/services/state_classifier.go`. For a read-only bash call under this adapter, each is dead for a *cited* reason:

| rule | why it cannot fire |
|---|---|
| `permission_prompt` (hook tier, `PermissionPending`) | copilot ships **no hooks at all** — `agent.go` declares a single `KindObserve` permission ("Read session transcripts") and no hook installer, so nothing can ever set the hook-tier flag |
| `transcript_permission_prompt` (`TranscriptPermissionPending`) | set only by `applyPermissionDeltas` folding a `permission.requested` id into `openPermissions` (tailer.go:964 → tailer_metrics.go:475). The auto-approved call writes no such line — the live evidence above |
| `user_blocking_tool` (`NeedsUserAttention`) | requires an OPEN tool whose name is in `isUserBlockingTool` (metrics.go:450: `AskUserQuestion`/`ExitPlanMode`/`question`/`ask_user_question`). Copilot's tool here is `bash` |
| `open_tool_stalled` (`OpenToolStalled`) | requires `isPermissionGatedEditTool` (metrics.go:497: edit/write/multiedit/notebookedit/write_file). `bash` is deliberately excluded — it can legitimately run for minutes |
| `idle_prompt` (`IdlePromptPending`) | Claude Code's Notification hook only; inert for every non-hook adapter |

So the arc is forced: `user.message` → `working`, tool events are continued activity, `assistant.turn_end` → `turn_done` → `agent_done` → `ready`. The scenario's safe-path invariant ("state never entered waiting") is not merely observed, it is unreachable — which is the strongest form this assertion can take.

## What `session.permissions_changed` actually carries (checked, not assumed)

This event type exists live and the parser has no arm for it (it falls to `default: Skip`). It is **not** an auto-classification record and is not this cell's signal. Read from `51ffced3-…/events.jsonl` line 2, immediately after `session.start`:

```json
{"type":"session.permissions_changed","data":{"previousAllowAllPermissions":false,"allowAllPermissions":true,"previousAllowAllPermissionMode":"off","allowAllPermissionMode":"on"}}
```

It records the **allow-all mode toggle** — the `--allow-all` / `COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL` blanket switch going on or off. Per-call classifier verdicts are never written; the only trace of a decision is the presence or absence of `permission.requested`. Skipping it is therefore correct for state, and its one latent use is diagnostic: its absence in `40dfdd13-…` is part of the proof that session ran without `--allow-all`. Worth revisiting only if a future cell wants to assert the mode itself (a mid-session toggle would be invisible today) — a caveat, not a bug: nothing this scenario asserts depends on it.

## The launch decision, made deliberately

The cell is recorded with **`COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1`**, i.e. WITHOUT `--allow-all`. With the flag on, every call is pre-approved and the recording would be indistinguishable from `2-2 auto-executed-tool-call` — the same transcript, the same arc, and no evidence that a classifier exists. Dropping it is what makes the fixture assert the thing the scenario is named for. This is not a driver gap: `replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh:179-180` already gates the flag behind that env var (added for the 2-19 sibling), and line 303 gates `dismiss_dialog_if_visible` behind the same var — so under this cell's configuration `wait_turn` will NOT silently answer an unexpected prompt; it would hang to timeout and fail the cell honestly. Both behaviours are what this cell wants.

## Relationship to the neighbouring cells

- `2-2 auto-executed-tool-call` — same arc, but with `--allow-all`; it asserts "a tool call doesn't disturb the arc", not "the agent classified it".
- `2-19 tool-gate-permission-prompt` — the risky branch of this same scenario, recorded to `waiting` and left there. This cell deliberately captures ONLY the safe branch, exactly as the claudecode sibling does (its spec says so in as many words), because a single recipe cannot both terminate in `waiting` and settle to `ready`.
caveats: RECORDING PRECONDITION (deliberate, and the whole point of the cell): record with COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1 so copilot launches WITHOUT --allow-all. With --allow-all every call is pre-approved and the no-waiting result would be an artifact of the launch flags rather than evidence of the agent's classifier — the recording would be a duplicate of 2-2. The lever already exists (driver-interactive.sh:180); nothing needs porting.

PROVISIONAL — the exact command's classification (emission, not parsing): the recipe asks for `ls -la`, whereas the live-verified auto-approvals were `cat data.txt` and `cat probe.txt`. The inference is that `ls` shares the shape the classifier cleared (a read-only identifier, hasWriteFileRedirection=false, paths inside the trusted cwd), but Copilot's classifier lives in the native core (app.js only relays `readOnly` through to the permission payload), so no allow-list is readable from the binary. If `ls` unexpectedly prompts, the recording FAILS LOUDLY (a waiting transition, and wait_turn will not dismiss the dialog under COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL) — the fix is then to swap the prompt to `cat` over a file, which requires the driver to seed one in the run cwd (there is no shell step type). This is the main reason confidence is 0.85 and not higher.

The recipe must end on a DECLARATIVE reply ('reply with just: done'). A turn ending on a prose question routes to waiting through agent_done → classifyAgentDone — proven for this very adapter in the 2-17 user-blocking-question cell — which would violate this cell's invariant for a reason that has nothing to do with permissions.

COPILOT WRITES TWO assistant.turn_end EVENTS PER PROMPT when a tool is involved (verified in 40dfdd13 and a030ac38: turn_start → tool → turn_end, then turn_start → text → turn_end), and each maps to turn_done → agent_done → ready. A brief ready blip mid-prompt is therefore expected, and the spec is built to tolerate it: the no-waiting invariant is carried by a `kind`-anchored phase (whose duration_at_least_ms defines only the invariant window — checkDurationAtLeast is skipped when expected_state is empty, expected.go:685) rather than by a `working` phase with a long duration, which a ready blip would fail. It also means wait_turn returns at the FIRST turn_end, before the closing text turn — hence the trailing sleep.

OBSERVATIONS assert cost/tokens non-zero, mirroring the 2-2 sibling (assistant.message.outputTokens is Copilot's live token signal). A BYOK recording (COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL/_API_KEY + COPILOT_MODEL) reports totalNanoAiu 0 and a model name outside irrlicht's priced alias map, so cost would land at zero: record this cell against the real Copilot backend, or let record correct the observation. model is deliberately unpinned — --model accepts only 'auto' on this account and the router picks per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5.

BIRTH RE-ANCHORED from the live recording 2026-08-03: the transient proc-<PID> presession is born ready, but the REAL session is born DIRECTLY into working (state_transition new_state=working, reason "new session created") — copilot writes events.jsonl only at the first prompt, so the open turn is already on disk at discovery. session_birth and turn_start are therefore ONE phase (first_turn_start); the pre-recording spec asserted a ready birth followed by a separate ready→working, a shape that no longer exists.

VACUITY WARNING WITHDRAWN 2026-08-03: the previous recording of this cell was flagged vacuous because session.MergeMetrics dropped TranscriptPermissionPending, so no copilot session could reach waiting from the transcript at all and the load-bearing `no state_transition to waiting` invariant passed for the wrong reason. That bug is fixed (commit "fix(session): carry TranscriptPermissionPending through MergeMetrics") and the sibling cell 2-19 tool-gate-permission-prompt was re-recorded green on the SAME daemon build, live-emitting a waiting transition with decided_by_rule=transcript_permission_prompt. The invariant is therefore discriminating again. This re-recording also carries the independent transcript-level evidence: tool.execution_start/tool.execution_complete for the bash call with NO permission.requested line anywhere, and no session.permissions_changed enabling allowAllPermissions — i.e. COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL was honoured and the read-only call was classified, not pre-approved.

RESOLVED — the `ls -la` classification is no longer provisional: the 2026-08-03 recording shows the recipe's `ls -la` bash call executing with tool.execution_start/tool.execution_complete and raising NO permission.requested, confirming the classifier clears it exactly like the `cat` calls the assessment inferred from.

sources.note: THE load-bearing evidence, live on CLI 1.0.77: one session, two prompts. `cat data.txt` → tool.execution_start (shellToolInfo.hasWriteFileRedirection=false) → tool.execution_complete with NO permission.requested between them; `echo written > out.txt` → permission.requested {kind:shell, commands:[{identifier:echo, readOnly:true}], possiblePaths:[out.txt], hasWriteFileRedirection:true} and a 35 s block. The write prompting proves --allow-all was off, so the read-only auto-approval is the agent's own classification.

Second instance of the same shape and the timing basis for the recipe: `cat probe.txt` auto-executed (no permission event), whole prompt user.message → first assistant.turn_end in 4.5 s, closing text turn 1.4 s later, then session.usage_checkpoint.

The session.permissions_changed line (line 2, right after session.start): previousAllowAllPermissions false → allowAllPermissions true, permission MODE off → on. Establishes that this event carries the blanket allow-all toggle, not a per-call classifier verdict — so the parser's default Skip is correct and no auto-classification record exists on disk.

The five rules that can decide `waiting` (permission_prompt:114, transcript_permission_prompt:153, user_blocking_tool:160, open_tool_stalled:173, idle_prompt:187) — the enumeration behind the structural-unreachability argument, plus agent_done:202 which supplies the working→ready settle from assistant.turn_end.

isUserBlockingTool (line 450: AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode/question/ask_user_question) and isPermissionGatedEditTool (line 497: edit/write/multiedit/notebookedit/write_file, with bash deliberately excluded) — why neither the user_blocking_tool nor the open_tool_stalled rule can fire on a Copilot `bash` call.
Permissions = one KindObserve entry ('Read session transcripts'); no hook installer anywhere in the adapter — so the hook-tier PermissionPending rule has no producer for this agent and cannot fire.

Dispatch table (lines 85-118): tool.execution_start → function_call, tool.execution_complete → function_call_output, assistant.turn_end → turn_done, permission.requested/completed → the permission ids. The default arm's comment lists exactly what is skipped — session.permissions_changed falls there.
Line 475: TranscriptPermissionPending = len(openPermissions) > 0 — the only producer of the transcript-tier waiting flag, and it stays empty for a turn with no permission.requested.

Lines 179-181: `local args=(--no-color)` with `[[ -z ${COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL:-} ]] && args+=(--allow-all)` — the lever this cell sets, already implemented. Line 303 gates dismiss_dialog_if_visible behind the same var, so wait_turn cannot silently answer an unexpected prompt in this configuration. DRIVE_ELICITS (line 128) lists send/wait_turn/sleep. turn_count (283) counts assistant.turn_end, so wait_turn returns at the first of the two.

sources.ref: copilot --help (CLI 1.0.77, read from app.js option table)
sources.note: --allow-all: 'Enable all permissions (equivalent to --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls)'; --allow-all-tools: 'Allow all tools to run automatically without confirmation' (env COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL). The documented reason --allow-all would make this cell's assertion vacuous.

Scanned for the classifier's allow-list: the only `readOnly` occurrences are payload plumbing (MCP onPermission, the ACP permission mapper, tool-registry metadata). The decision itself is made in the native core (h.sessionPlan* bindings), so no readable allow-list exists — which is why the safe/gated split is asserted from live transcripts rather than from strings.
The sibling this cell mirrors: it too captures ONLY the safe branch and states that the risky branch belongs to tool-gate-permission-prompt.

checkDurationAtLeast (685) returns early when ExpectedState is empty, and checkPhaseInvariants (711) uses matched.Ts..+DurationAtLeastMs as the invariant window; findMatchingEvent (623) admits an event AT the anchor timestamp. Together these are why a `kind`-anchored phase can pin the no-waiting invariant across the whole turn without a ready blip failing it.

preconditions: copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login)

An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this recording spends them. Do NOT record this cell over BYOK: totalNanoAiu is 0 and the BYOK model name falls outside irrlicht's priced alias map, so the cost observation would land at zero

COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL=1 MUST be exported for this cell so the driver launches copilot WITHOUT --allow-all. This is the whole point: with --allow-all everything is pre-approved and the recording proves nothing about the agent's classifier (it would duplicate 2-2 auto-executed-tool-call)
irrlicht's copilot `transcripts` permission granted (IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all for the recorder) — a fresh IRRLICHT_HOME leaves it pending and the daemon observes nothing
tmux available (the interactive driver drives the REPL through it). No hook install and no :7837 pinning — the whole signal is transcript-borne, so the coexist recorder on :7838 captures it
setup: The driver isolates state under $STAGING/copilot-home via COPILOT_HOME and seeds trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals so neither first-run modal blocks the input box, then waits for the '/ commands' footer before typing
A fresh per-run cwd under <staging>/cwd/. The requested command reads only that directory, so it needs no seeded fixture — deliberate, because no step type can create one
Recommended: export COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS=bash. The driver forwards it as --available-tools=bash, dropping ~8.3k of ~12k input tokens and roughly halving what this cell costs

Under COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL the driver also skips dismiss_dialog_if_visible inside wait_turn, so an unexpected permission prompt would hang to timeout rather than being silently answered — the failure this cell wants to be loud
Interactive, not headless: the REPL must outlive the turn so the daemon observes the working→ready settle rather than a process exit

script.text: Run the shell command `ls -la` with the bash tool, then reply with just: done

verify: events.jsonl shows a transient proc-<PID> presession born ready, then the real session (the session-state directory name — a DIFFERENT id) born ready when the transcript appears
events.jsonl shows a ready→working transition for the real session when the prompt is sent, and a working→ready settle by the end of the run; final session state is ready
events.jsonl contains NO state_transition to waiting for any session during the whole run

THE TRANSCRIPT-LEVEL ASSERTION THAT CANNOT BE FOOLED BY TIMING: the recorded events.jsonl contains at least one tool.execution_start / tool.execution_complete pair for the bash tool AND NO permission.requested line at all. A missing waiting transition alone could in principle be a sampling artifact; an absent permission.requested is the agent's classifier verdict written down

the recorded transcript shows the run launched without --allow-all — i.e. no session.permissions_changed line turning allowAllPermissions on (its presence means COPILOT_NO_ALLOW_ALL was not honoured and the cell is vacuous, whatever the pass rate says)
the newest recording's replay summary shows cum_output_tokens > 0 and estimated_cost_usd > 0, with model_name one of gpt-5-mini / claude-haiku-4.5 (router's choice — not pinned)
